question: What is the primary purpose of the Essential Drug Programme?

options.A: To manufacture all required pharmaceuticals locally
options.B: To ensure availability of affordable and safe medicines
options.C: To provide free luxury medications for public officials
options.D: To eliminate the use of herbal remedies entirely

explanation: The core objective of the programme is making sure that population health needs are met through accessible, safe, and cost-effective pharmaceutical supplies. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h1)

question: How does an essential drug list primarily help a resource-limited health system?

options.A: By completely removing the need for qualified pharmacists
options.B: By increasing the total volume of imported brand-name drugs
options.C: By optimizing financial resources and procurement efficiency
options.D: By stopping all pharmaceutical research and development

explanation: Focusing purchasing power on a select group of high-priority medicines prevents budget wastage on redundant or marginally beneficial alternatives. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h1)

question: In which year did the World Health Organization release its first Model List of Essential Medicines?
explanation: The landmark WHO model list was introduced in 1977 to guide countries in selecting cost-effective treatments for prevalent diseases. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h2)

question: What led the WHO to introduce the concept of essential medicines?

options.A: A sudden surplus of chemical manufacturing factories globally
options.B: A mandate from private pharmaceutical corporations
options.C: The complete eradication of infectious diseases in developing nations
options.D: Widespread market confusion and financial drainage from unproven drugs

explanation: Unregulated markets packed with redundant, expensive brand-name products necessitated a standardized international approach to medicine selection. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h2)

question: Which factor is foundational when selecting a drug based on public health relevance?

options.A: Whether the drug has a celebrity endorsement
options.B: The country of origin of the raw chemical
options.D: The aesthetic packaging of the medication

explanation: Public health relevance dictates that medicines chosen must address the actual disease burden experienced by the local population. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h3)

question: Why is cost-effectiveness evaluated beyond just the initial unit purchase price of a medicine?

options.A: Because total treatment success and duration influence overall expenses
options.B: Because government taxes change every single week
options.C: Because cheap drugs never require storage facilities
options.D: Because shipping fees are always higher than manufacturing costs

explanation: A cheaper unit price may result in higher overall costs if a drug has low efficacy, leading to prolonged illness or treatment failure. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of drug standardization in a health system?

options.A: To prevent nurses from administering intravenous fluids
options.B: To increase the cost of specialized hospital care
options.C: To ensure every single brand in the world is imported
options.D: To limit therapeutic duplication and simplify inventory

explanation: Standardization reduces the confusion of stocking multiple drugs with identical pharmacological effects, streamlining both supply chains and clinical practice. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h4)

question: A pharmacotherapeutic committee decides to drop a newly patented drug in favor of an older, well-studied alternative with equal efficacy. What guiding principle supports this decision?

options.A: A strict ban on all modern medical technology
options.B: Evidence-based cost-effectiveness and proven safety data
options.C: The personal preference of the hospital administrator
options.D: An intention to lower the morale of medical doctors

explanation: Older medications often have extensive safety profiles and lower costs without sacrificing therapeutic benefit compared to expensive newer alternatives. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h4)

question: What is the official title of the document that guides public pharmaceutical procurement in Nigeria?
explanation: The NEML is the official Nigerian policy tool dictating standard pharmaceutical selections for public health institutions. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h5)

question: A state health board in Nigeria is reviewing its drug supply requisition for secondary hospitals. Which guideline should strictly inform their purchasing decisions?

options.C: Personal recommendations from pharmaceutical sales reps

explanation: Public sector procurement must align directly with the NEML to ensure funds are spent on nationally prioritized, evidence-based treatments. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a core component of the drug supply chain?
explanation: Unregulated street vending undermines the pharmaceutical supply chain and poses severe safety hazards; formal supply chains rely on structured procurement and distribution. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h6)

question: What is a primary consequence of poor inventory management in a public hospital pharmacy?

options.A: Enhanced therapeutic compliance among chronic disease patients
options.B: An immediate surplus of financial revenue for infrastructural expansion
options.C: Automatic upgrading of the facility to a tertiary medical center
options.D: Stock-outs of critical life-saving drugs and medication wastage from expiration

explanation: Inaccurate forecasting and tracking frequently cause either devastating shortages of vital medicines or large batches expiring on shelves. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h6)

question: What is the primary danger associated with irrational antibiotic use and incomplete dosing regimens?

options.B: Immediate reduction in hospital electricity tariffs

explanation: Misuse and under-dosing of anti-infective agents allow resistant microbial strains to survive and proliferate, threatening public health. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h7)

question: Why is polypharmacy discouraged within the framework of rational drug use?

options.A: It guarantees that pharmaceutical companies will lower their prices
options.B: It ensures that patients swallow fewer tablets each morning
options.C: It increases the risk of adverse drug interactions and medication errors
options.D: It simplifies the nurse's daily documentation workload

explanation: Prescribing excessive, unneeded medications complicates treatment regimens and raises the likelihood of harmful drug-drug interactions and toxicity. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h7)

question: Which agency in Nigeria receives reports regarding adverse drug reactions through nurse-led pharmacovigilance?
explanation: The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) is the regulatory body responsible for drug safety and pharmacovigilance in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h8)

question: A patient on a ward experiences an unexpected skin rash and respiratory wheezing immediately following intravenous administration of a standard essential antibiotic. What is the most appropriate immediate action for the attending nurse?

options.A: Discharge the patient from the hospital without documenting the event
options.B: Stop the infusion immediately, maintain airway patency, and report the adverse reaction
options.C: Ignore the symptom because the drug is listed on the National Essential Medicines List
options.D: Increase the infusion rate to clear the drug from the intravenous tubing faster

explanation: Patient safety is paramount; halting the offending agent, managing acute symptoms, and reporting adverse events are core nursing responsibilities. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h8)
